stem: (Select TWO.) Orchid Logistics commits `.terraform.lock.hcl` and wants every CI run to install the identical release of a registry module. Which two statements are accurate?

choices.text: The lock file records provider selections only, and it does not remember which module release was chosen
Committing the lock file freezes the module release, because it lists every external dependency
Writing an exact `version = "6.0.1"` in the module block holds the module to that single release
A range such as `version = "~> 6.0"` keeps the first release installed on every later run
A `!=` condition in the constraint holds the module to a single release

rationale: At present the dependency lock file tracks only provider dependencies, and Terraform does not remember version selections for remote modules. The documented way to freeze a module is an exact version constraint, which always selects the same release. Committing the lock file does not freeze a module because it holds no module entries. A range constraint can move to a newer release the next time Terraform selects a version, because nothing remembers the first pick. The `!=` operator only excludes one exact version; it does not hold the module to a single release.
